about: Soft-tissue secondary-motion data for AnthroForge characters. GLB/glTF carries no dynamics, so dynamics ship as DATA: spring-chain records + a paintable softness field. A runtime (Babylon app, Blender bake, VRM export) integrates the chains. Field names deliberately mirror the VRMC_springBone glTF extension so a VRM export maps 1:1. Full rationale + measured prototype numbers: SOFT_DYNAMICS.md in this folder.

chain_record._comment: One record per spring chain instance on a character.

fields.colliders: optional list of {bone, offset, radius} spheres the chain must not penetrate (thighs, belly wall)
fields.gravity_power: gravity multiplier (VRM 'gravityPower'); >1 for hyper masses whose visual weight should read heavier than the host's scale
fields.hit_radius: per-bone collision radius for runtime colliders (metres)
fields.part: part id the chain belongs to (PARTS_STANDARD record)
fields.rest_offsets: per-segment rest offset vectors in the root frame (metres)
fields.root_bone: bone the chain hangs from (its animated frame drives segment 1)

export_paths.babylon_app: runtime integrates chains live from these records (same integrator, TS port); AF_softness sampled per segment from the character's painted field at build time
export_paths.blender_bake: offline: run the integrator against an animation's root-bone matrices, write bone rotation fcurves (prototype_softdynamics.blend was built exactly this way; scripts/build_prototype.py is the reference implementation, verified 0.0 mm tip error vs the sim at checked frames)
export_paths.glb_plain: no dynamics in file (state this in the export profile so nobody expects sway from a bare GLB); baked variant available via blender_bake
export_paths.vrm: map to VRMC_springBone: stiffness/drag_force/gravity_power/hit_radius carry the same names and near-enough semantics; rest_offsets become joint rest local translations

hyper_animation._comment: SLOT for the parallel hyper-animation research wave (dynamics/hyper-animation/). Its per-part-class parameter tables (hyper bellies, hyper chest, multi-shaft sets, oversized tails at 2-4x authored ranges) merge into 'profiles' above when it lands; keys should be added as profiles.hyper_<part> entries with the same field shape. Nothing in this file blocks on it.

integrator.notes: Each segment is slerped toward its rest direction RELATIVE to its parent segment's current direction (segment 1: relative to the root bone's animated frame). This resists kinking, not swinging: hang angle and sway emerge from spring-vs-gravity balance, which is what makes settle time the honest stiffness readout. Positional (shape-matching) springs were prototyped first and rejected: they glue every particle to the rest pose and kill the pendulum mode (peak lag 1-2 deg on a walk cycle, no visible tissue behaviour).

profiles._comment: Starting parameter sets per part class. [S]=measured in the prototype, [D]=derived analytically, [E]=estimate for first builds to tighten. All stiffness values are for the verlet angular-spring integrator above at 30 fps x 4 substeps.

belly_apron.tier: [E] scaled from sac prototype toward firmer root

ear.tier: [E] ears are light; gravity_power <1 keeps them from dragging

hyper_sac_kaleaon_scale.tier: [D] analytic: 0.94 m hang -> pendulum period ~1.95 s, near stride resonance; 218 kg contents -> momentum-dominated, needs MORE drag, not more stiffness, or the sway runs away. See SOFT_DYNAMICS.md section 5.

sac.tier: [S] prototype SOFT setting: settle 1.60 s, equilibrium hang offset 7.1 deg, walk dynamic swing peak 4.2 deg on the wolf-scale stand-in (0.42 m chain)

sac_firm_variant.tier: [S] prototype FIRM setting: settle 0.43 s, hang offset 5.8 deg -- reads as a much smaller/tighter sac; use for lean builds

tail.tier: [E] tails are active (muscle) -- dynamics are a garnish on authored animation, keep stiffness mid

teat.tier: [S] prototype: 4.8 cm chains on the sac tip, peak swing 30-34 deg in walk (relative to the sac tip frame) -- teats flop visibly and settle fast; do NOT soften below the host chain or they free-flail (55-60 deg, measured)

softness_field.authoring_gradient_rule: softness increases monotonically from a part's root to its free end unless anatomy says otherwise (ear base firm, tip free; sac root firm, pole free).
softness_field.effective_stiffness_mapping: k_eff(segment) = k_chain * (1 - 0.6 * softness(segment)) * length_factor(segment); length_factor compensates pendulum frequency: short chains need less spring relief (prototype: 4.8 cm teat at softness 1.0 runs k_chain x 2.0 and lands at the same effective rate as designed; see SOFT_DYNAMICS.md section 4).
softness_field.name: AF_softness
softness_field.semantics: 0 = rigid core tissue (belly wall over muscle), 1 = freest soft tissue (teats, sac pole, ear tips). Painted like AF_mobility (gravity work) -- same brush discipline, different field.
softness_field.storage: per-vertex float (Blender vertex group in .blend/.target tooling; float attribute in GLB as a TEXCOORD-like custom attribute on export profiles that support it; always present in the .afchar sidecar data)
